title: Insurance Binders on Wayfare Driver Agreements: Desk Guidance and Recording Tool
content:
**Product:** Driver Services Agreements and Account Standing. **Subject:** recording an insurance binder a Wayfare driver has uploaded as auto insurance.

## Rule applied by the desk

An insurance binder uploaded to the driver's standing record is accepted as the auto insurance on file for its binder acceptance days, counted in calendar days from the day support records it. A binder updates the agreement only when support records it: the auto insurance expiry date on the agreement becomes the recording day plus the binder acceptance days, whatever end date is printed on the binder. Until support records it, an uploaded binder leaves the auto insurance expiry date on the agreement as it was.

The binder in question is the latest auto insurance upload on the standing record. Recording it is a support action; it is not a request the driver has to make.

## Standing of the agreement

The binder acceptance days are fixed only after the agreement's status and deactivation date already show any deactivation for document lapse that its document hold has run into.

Put the other way round, in the same terms: while an agreement's document hold has run into a deactivation for document lapse that its status and deactivation date do not yet show, the binder acceptance days are not yet fixed.

## Recording tool

The binder is recorded with the agent tool `record_insurance_binder_0f7a5736`. It is a hidden tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

- `driver_agreement_id`: the reference number of the driver services agreement whose insurance on file is being recorded, as returned by the driver agreement lookup.
- `accepted_days`: the binder's accepted period, as a whole number of calendar days counted from today (integer, no decimals, no unit text). The insurance expiry date on file becomes today plus that many days.

The tool takes today's date from the system clock as the recording day. One call changes only the agreement's insurance expiry date on file; nothing else on the agreement changes.

## Receipt

The tool returns a dictionary receipt with `driver_agreement_id` (the agreement reference number), `insurance_expiry_date` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, the insurance expiry date now on file) and `recorded_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`, today's date). A receipt carrying the new `insurance_expiry_date` means the binder is recorded, and the insurance counts as on file and unexpired through that date. The tool's contract defines no other outcome.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

Recorded on 2026-07-01 with an `accepted_days` of `38`, the receipt shows an `insurance_expiry_date` of `2026-08-08` and a `recorded_on` of `2026-07-01`.
